play.title: Half a Word
story: The Roman Forum was the heart of the old city.
Broken columns stand in the grass. Aldo sits on a stone and opens his bag.
"Show me Livia's drawing," he says. "Old maps used Latin words."
play.letter:
LATIN WORDS FOR ROOMS ON OLD MAPS
BIBLIOTHECA — a library, a room for books
BALNEUM — a bath, a room for washing
THEATRUM — a theatre, a place for shows
play.question: What kind of room is on the real piece?
hints: Look at the half word on Livia's drawing. How does it start?
The room also has lines like shelves. What do shelves hold?
play.successMessage: You read the old Latin word!
transition: "A Roman library, never found," Aldo whispers. "That would be amazing."
"But where was it? Let's follow the street on the map."

play.title: Walk the Old Street
story: On Livia's drawing, a long street runs to the library.
Aldo moves his finger along it, slowly.
"Listen carefully," he says. "I will read it like a story."
play.letter:
The old street starts at the Forum.
The library is at the end of the street. It is in a small square with an owl.
Just before the owl square, the street passes a long market.
Between the Forum and the market, there is a round temple.
play.question: Put the places on the old street in order, from the Forum.
hints: Find the start and the end first.
Between means in the middle of two places.
transition: Forum, round temple, long market, owl square.
"The temple and the market are still there today," says Aldo.
"So the owl square must be just after the market. What is it called now?"
play.orderFeedback: Start at the Forum and end at the owl square. Then read Between and Just before.

play.title: Aldo's Map Cabinet
story: Aldo's map archive is full of long, flat drawers.
His newest city plans are in a cabinet with three dials.
"I use the old street's marker stones as my code," he says. "Can you read them?"
play.letter:
My code: the old street's three marker stones, in order from the Forum.

THE MARKER STONES ON LIVIA'S DRAWING:
at the market — VI
at the temple — IV
at the owl square — IX

ROMAN NUMBERS: I = 1, V = 5, X = 10.
A small number before a big one means take away: IV = 5 - 1.
A small number after a big one means add: VI = 5 + 1.
play.question: Turn the dials to the three marker stones, in order from the Forum.
hints: Walk the street from the Forum: which place comes first?
IX: the I is before the X. So take one away from ten.
transition: Inside is the city's plan for Piazza della Civetta.
"CONCRETE WILL BE POURED ON 10 MAY, AT 7 AM."
Livia grabs your arm. "That is in two days! The library will be covered forever!"

feedback.649: Start at the Forum. Which marker stone comes first on the street?
feedback.459: VI has the small number after the big one: 5 + 1.

play.orderFeedback: Right numbers, wrong order. Walk the street from the Forum.
